grade.reason: The agent's change to the UDP branch of `_get_client_hello` in `mitmproxy/addons/next_layer.py` is identical to the merged upstream code change. It gates QUIC parsing on `_starts_like_quic` and DTLS parsing on `starts_like_dtls_record`. The upstream changelog and test edits are not needed for functional equivalence.

result:
I changed `_get_client_hello` in `mitmproxy/addons/next_layer.py` so QUIC flows no longer stall when `allow_hosts` or `ignore_hosts` is set. I haven't run any tests, and I didn't add one.

For UDP, the function now only tries to parse a QUIC ClientHello if `_starts_like_quic(...)` says the data plausibly is QUIC. It only tries the DTLS parse if `starts_like_dtls_record(...)` says so. This matches what the TCP branch already does with `starts_like_tls_record`.

Previously, the empty `b""` data seen right after the QUIC TLS handshake failed both parsers with `ValueError`. That got turned into `NeedsMoreData`, so `_next_layer` bailed out every time. Now that data fails the heuristics, `_get_client_hello` returns `None`. The host check then falls back to `context.client.sni`, and the flow gets its layer.

I didn't add a test. A natural one would call `_get_client_hello` with a UDP context and `b""` and expect `None` instead of `NeedsMoreData`.
